mainEntity.name: How do I stop AI from making up facts, sources, or statistics in my slides?

acceptedAnswer.text: Begin with authoritative sources, a defined scope, and explicit instructions not to invent facts, citations, statistics, or quotations. Then verify every important claim against the supplied material and a reliable independent source before publication. Run My AI Biz’s workflows include source verification and safeguards against unsupported proof or income claims. Context: fluent wording can make an incorrect statement appear credible, especially in history, science, health, finance, or business education. Key factors: topic risk, source quality, date sensitivity, numerical content, quotations, and whether the audience can detect errors. Practical guidance: maintain a claim-and-source table for important slides, mark uncertain points for review, and remove claims that cannot be confirmed. Ask the system to show where each statement came from, but do not treat its explanation as proof. A human subject-matter reviewer should approve high-consequence content.
acceptedAnswer.description: Provide reliable source material, instruct the system not to invent claims, and verify every important statement independently. Keep a claim-and-source checklist, especially for numbers, quotations, dates, and high-stakes subjects.
